root_cause.text: In `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2()`, the ID blob is copied to userspace regardless of whether the PSP firmware command (SEV_GET_ID2) failed, so when the firmware returns an error indicating the userspace buffer is too small and updates the length to the required size, the kernel copies more bytes than allocated, causing an out-of-bounds read from the kernel-allocated buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free;` before the `copy_to_user()`, and the commit message states: "If the failure was due to an invalid length, i.e. the userspace buffer+length was too small, copying the number of bytes _firmware_ requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace." The KASAN report confirms a slab-out-of-bounds read during `copy_to_user`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to abort the operation when an error has already occurred, avoiding potential data leakage or corruption.
intent_record.what: Added an if statement checking if 'ret' is non-zero or if 'argp->error' is non-zero (with WARN_ON_ONCE), and if so, jumps to the 'e_free' label to free resources and exit.
intent_record.how: This change prevents the function from proceeding to copy data to user space if an error has already been indicated, either by a non-zero return code or by the error field in the command structure. It also triggers a kernel warning if 'argp->error' is set, aiding in debugging.

candidates.rationale: This copy_to_user call uses data.len, which may have been updated by the PSP firmware to a larger required size even when the SEV_GET_ID2 command fails. Without a guard to abort on firmware error, this copies more bytes than allocated from the kernel buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read.

vuln_statements.explanation: This copy_to_user call uses data.len as the size, which may have been updated by the PSP firmware to a larger required size even when the SEV_GET_ID2 command fails. Without a prior check on the firmware command's return status, an error causes out-of-bounds read from the id_blob kernel buffer when copied to userspace.
